entries.title: The Brewers own the Cubs — it's just reality
entries.summary: <p>Another year, another “own” goal in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a>-Brewers rivalry.</p><p>Actually, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/05/20/brewers-cubs-jacob-misiorowski-christian-yelich-pete-crow-armstrong-wrigley-field-mlb" target="_blank" >make that the Brewers-Cubs rivalry</a>. No doubt, the Brewers deserve to be named first. There’s no team they enjoy leaving in the National League Central dust more than the Cubs, and wouldn’t you know it? They’ve all but done it again.</p><p>There’s no easy or nice way to say it, but it’s the truth: The North-of-the-Border Nine owns our North Siders.</p><p>The Brewers showed up Monday for the opener of a four-game series at Wrigley Field with the best record in the big leagues and a bullyish eight-game lead over the second-place Cubs, who almost certainly will soon be 0-for-3 in the division-winning department since Craig Counsell switched sides to become the sport’s first $8 million-a-year manager.</p><p>Worse than that, it stands to be the eighth straight full season — the exception being the pandemic-shortened 60-game sprint in 2020 — in which the Cubs will finish behind the Brewers, who are closing in on their sixth division crown during the most dominant stretch of baseball in franchise history.</p><p>“Look, we get 13 chances to play the Brewers,” Counsell said, his team off to a 2-4 start in the season series. “And other than that, we don’t have any control over the Brewers. They’ve got to go play their games, and we go play our games.”</p><p>If the implication is that the rivals’ records might be closer if they played each other 162 times, it’s hard to fathom why they would be.</p><p>“They’re on pace for a big number — they’re on over a 100-win pace — and that’s hard to keep up with,” Counsell said. “Go ask the rest of major league baseball.”</p><p>No one in Cubdom has to ask anybody. To put the bullying in perspective, think back to the mercilessly one-sided decades of Brett Favre, Aaron Rodgers and the Packers owning the Bears and know the last time the Packers had the better record eight times in nine years was from 1992 to 2000. Still too fresh for Bears fans, no doubt, but kind of a long time ago.</p><p>Counsell didn’t come here to lose to his former team. His boss, Jed Hoyer, didn’t stake his own reputation on an all-in managerial hire just to go oh-fer in division races. Counsell has a couple of years left after this one, and the Cubs are positioned to continue to be a playoff-caliber team. But there’s no sign of the Brewers losing their mojo and fading away.</p><p>I asked Counsell how disappointed and/or frustrated he is that the Cubs haven’t been able to close the gap on his watch.</p><p>“ ‘Disappointed’ is not the right word,” he said. “They’re good. They’re a good team. I’m not surprised by that, not surprised at all. We’re a good team. We’re not a 100-win team — we’re not going to be a 100-win team this year — but we’re a good team. So that’s the story right now, and we’ve got games in front of us.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">The <a href="https://x.com/Cubs?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@Cubs</a> go back-to-back!<br><br>Now Nico Hoerner leaves the yard 💪 <a href="https://t.co/P55cpzyhuS">https://t.co/P55cpzyhuS</a> <a href="https://t.co/DKEgZ6pb6b">pic.twitter.com/DKEgZ6pb6b</a></p>— MLB (@MLB) <a href="https://x.com/MLB/status/2094575296594788766?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 31, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Cubs finished 10 games behind the Brewers and missed the playoffs in 2024, Counsell’s first season. The gap was smaller — five games — last year, but the Brewers’ postseason series win against the Cubs underscored an undeniable hierarchy.</p><p>This season, the low point for the Cubs was a 10-game losing streak in May during which they were swept by the Brewers in three lopsided games — combined score, 19-5 — at Wrigley. The Brewers torched starter Shota Imanaga for eight earned runs in an opening 9-3 win that was reminiscent, right down to the final score, of the Brewers’ 9-3 win in Game 1 of last year’s NL division series, when they jumped on starter Matthew Boyd and the Cubs for six first-inning runs. Both games were like early-years Mike Tyson knockouts.</p><p>As Brewers manager Pat Murphy told his players going into that playoff series, “When the bell rings, you’re ready. You don’t get a couple rounds to figure out whether or not you want to fight.”</p><p>Before the Cubs’ 10-game losing streak this year, they were in first place by 2½ games over the Brewers. By the end of it, they were in last place, 4½ games behind an uncanny powerhouse that never seems to fail to take advantage of openings and opportunities. The same has happened as the Cubs hit a little 3-7 jag entering the teams’ current series; over that same period, the Brewers kept plowing ahead at 7-3, doubling their lead from four to eight.</p><p>On the eve of Opening Day this season, I spoke with Christian Yelich, the longest-tenured Brewer, in Milwaukee. As is the case most years, the Cubs were projected to win more games. Yelich scoffed.</p><p>“I think a lot of people have been really waiting for the day that we suck and they can finally say, ‘We told you so, they’re no good,’ ” he said. “We’ve become accustomed to winning and being a postseason team. … That’s definitely not changing this year.”</p><p>Murphy — who has an excellent shot at a third straight NL manager of the year award — wasn’t backing down from a brawl in the slightest, either, five months ago.</p><p>“Buckle up and get ready,” he said, “because it’s going to be a fight. There’ll be a lot of bloodshed and pain to get to where you want to go.”</p><p>It sometimes seems the Cubs are less driven than the Brewers are to finish at the top of the standings.</p><p>“I think what motivates our group is playing good baseball and winning as many games as we can, and that’s been a constant since we’ve been together,” Ian Happ, the longest-tenured Cub, said Monday. “It’s always kind of the guiding light. You want to win divisions. You really want to win divisions — it means a lot — but playoff baseball is the important part.”</p><p>But the bullies have the Cubs bloodied again.</p><p>Getting a bit old, is it not?</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/31/cubs-brewers-phillies-nl-central-nl-wild-card-standings-diamondbacks-padres-mlb-playoffs-first-round" >Next two weeks give Cubs opportunity to make NL Central push vs. Brewers, but wild-card fate in balance, too</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/05/20/brewers-cubs-jacob-misiorowski-christian-yelich-pete-crow-armstrong-wrigley-field-mlb" >It’s Reality Week at Wrigley Field, where determined Brewers outclassed Cubs. What else is new?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2025/10/11/cubs-2025-postseason-runs-with-game-5-loss-to-brewers-in-nld" target="_blank" >Cubs’ 2025 postseason run ends with Game 5 loss to Brewers in NLDS</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Man fatally shot on Lower West Side
entries.summary: <p>A man was fatally shot Monday evening on the Lower West Side, police said.</p><p>The man, 35, was sitting on the front porch of a residence in the 2300 block of West 18th Place just before 7 p.m. when a car approached and someone got out and fired shots, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The man was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital with gunshot wounds to the chest. He was pronounced dead at the hospital.</p><p>No one is in custody and detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: After competing for a rotation spot in spring, Sean Newcomb has been invaluable in White Sox bullpen
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON – Protecting a one-run lead for four innings on Saturday, with relief ace Grant Taylor unavailable after working a career-high 2 2/3 frames on Friday, there were no easy answers for White Sox manager Will Venable.</p><p>Unless the answer was a lot of Sean Newcomb.</p><p>“I was talking with [general manager’ Chris Getz about it yesterday, about how valuable these guys are,” said Venable. “[Newcomb] leads the way. That prototype of pitchers, where he’s really good, he takes the ball all the time and [is] giving me two or three innings when he does pitch. It’s special.”</p><p>For the third time this year, and the second-straight outing, Newcomb posted three scoreless innings, helping push the Sox to 24-20 in one-run games. Newcomb’s logged 11 outings since he last allowed an earned run, spanning 20 1/3 innings. The streak has dropped his season ERA to 2.19, while working the third-most relief innings in the American League.</p><p>“You come out of the game and you see him coming in, you feel good about it,” said Sox starter Sean Burke.</p><p>An exciting young offensive core has powered this Sox team to the AL Central lead. But <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/31/white-sox-manager-will-venable-excited-to-bring-tommy-pham-jordan-leasure-mike-vasil-jose-urquidy-chris-getz-jake-cave-tyler-schweitzer-brenton-doyle-everson-pereira" target="_blank" ><u>Jordan Leasure and Mike Vasil were lost to season-ending elbow injuries</u></a> after being valuable setup men last year. Free-agent signing Seranthony Domínguez washed out as closer before being flipped at the deadline. Fireballer Jordan Hicks spent most of the first half battling a lat strain and searching for the right arm slot.</p><p>Protecting the leads of the AL’s best offense would be a tricky problem without a 33-year-old left-hander signed to a one-year, $4.5 million deal just before last Christmas, putting together arguably his finest season.</p><p>“Numbers-wise, can’t argue that,” Newcomb told the Sun-Times. “I'd say it’s a continuation of what I started doing with the A's when I got to a full-time bullpen job last year.”</p><p>Newcomb posted a 1.75 ERA in 51 1/3 innings for the A’s, after being designated for assignment midseason by his hometown Boston Red Sox, who had been using him as more of a spot starter/swingman. He credits that experience for why he has the stamina to maintain his performance even while on pace for over 90 innings this year.</p><p>What deserves possibly more credit is that in his 10th MLB season, on his fifth MLB team, after plenty of years dogged by injury and/or struggles, Newcomb is unfazed by anything.</p><p>“It’s been a new mindset I’ve had with pitching since I got back to playing consistently,” Newcomb said. “Just approaching every pitch the same way, no matter what it is.”</p><p>At a long-limbed six-foot-five and throwing from a lower arm slot than earlier in his career, Newcomb splits the plate horizontally with his slurve and a new sinker. That east-west dynamic has helped make the letter-high four-seam fastballs he peppers in to change eye levels one of the most effective pitches in the sport.</p><p>Part of Newcomb’s extended relief excellence are tools usually reserved for starters. When the situation calls for a groundball, or when it calls for a strikeout, Newcomb can hunt for either. When he misfires a four-seamer, he gets back into the count with a sinker, or vice-versa. Forget about his curveball, changeup or cutter, and that’s when they might appear.</p><p>For all the problems he’s solved in relief, maybe he would have done pretty well in that rotation job he wanted and competed for in spring.</p><p>“I haven’t weighed that in my head,” conceded Venable. “You have the argument to make that case. At the same time, he’s been so good and helped us win so many games, we are utilizing him well.”</p><p>But Newcomb is set to hit free agency again this winter, a forum where starting is markedly more valuable than relieving. Surely he’s more convinced in his ability to do the former than ever?</p><p>“No, same as always,” said Newcomb, true to his mindset.</p>
entries.author: James Fegan

entries.title: Cubs’ aggressive additions could prove key to finally clearing Brewers-shaped hurdle, now or in October
entries.summary: <p>If you can’t beat ‘em, add ‘em?</p><p>Even after luring <b>Craig Counsell</b> away, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> have yet to wrest control of the division from the Brewers.</p><p>But with another ex-Brewer in the fold, maybe things could be different?</p><p><b>Tyrone Taylor</b>, a Brewer from 2019 to 2023, made the case with his first-inning home run Monday, the start of a Cubs home-run barrage in the opener of the teams’ four-game series.</p><p>Taylor was added in one of <b>Jed Hoyer</b>’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" >aggressive moves at the trade deadline</a>, that deal with the Mets landing Monday’s starter, <b>Clay Holmes</b>, with hopes of the righty propelling the Cubs to big things from the top of the rotation.</p><p>Hoyer & Co. likely weren’t thinking of Taylor, a reserve outfielder who brought a .368 average and a .432 on-base percentage as a Cub into Monday, as a middle-of-the-order presence, but that homer – his first in a Cubs uniform – came from the cleanup spot.</p><p>Sure, role players can be difference-makers, but the Cubs parted with No. 2 prospect <b>Jefferson Rojas</b> to nab Holmes, who looked worth the cost once more Monday, following up <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/26/cubs-walk-off-loss-diamondbacks-clay-holmes-kevin-gausman-daniel-palencia-jacob-webb-bullpen" >seven shutout innings against the Diamondbacks</a> with six more scoreless frames against the Brewers. He’s got a 1.55 ERA since being acquired.</p><p>Before all that, the Cubs spent $175 million to add third baseman <b>Alex Bregman</b>, whose <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/21/cubs-alex-bregman-playoffs-stats-world-series-dansby-swanson-carson-kelly-craig-counsell" >scorching summer</a> has only been overshadowed by <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b>’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/29/cubs-star-pete-crow-armstrong-hits-three-home-runs-to-bolster-mvp-case" >MVP push</a>. Bregman had a .967 OPS in his previous 42 games before homering twice in his first three at-bats Monday.</p><p>If the Cubs are going to finally clear the Brewers-shaped hurdle, be it in a surprise late-season rally in the division race or come the postseason, the front office’s aggressive work to add to the roster could prove the difference.</p><p><b>Sticking with Shota</b></p><p>The Cubs have no plans to remove lefty <b>Shota Imanaga</b> from their rotation following <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/30/chicago-cubs-shota-imanaga-three-homers-cincinnati-reds-craig-counsell-jody-davis-jon-lester-ed-howard-edward-cabrera" >a second straight clunker Sunday</a>.</p><p>Imanaga leaped into a tie for the major league lead in home runs allowed by surrendering a trio to the Reds, matching the 33 given up by <b>Jeffrey Springs</b> of the Athletics.</p><p>“Shota’s going to make his next start,” Counsell said Monday. “We’re going to continue to work on, like everybody, having him be more effective, be your best possible self and be as effective as you possibly can. That work never stops.</p><p>“We need Shota to be one of our guys.”</p><p>The choice to stick with Imanaga is no shock. Though he wrapped a rough August with a 5.96 ERA in five starts, including a pair of games in which he allowed three homers, that followed a terrific July (1.53 ERA in five starts) and a stretch of a 2.09 ERA in nine starts.</p><p>“Major League Baseball is an execution game,” Counsell said. “Shota has proven, at his best self, he’s a very good major league pitcher. He didn’t execute some things [Sunday] night.”</p><p>However, watching Imanaga serve up long balls brings to mind how his 2025 ended: He gave up 10 homers in September and wasn’t chosen to start the Cubs’ loss to the Brewers in Game 5 of the NLDS.</p><p><b>Murray? Present.</b></p><p>Infielder <b>B.J. Murray Jr.</b> is joining the Cubs after putting up impressive numbers in the minors this season.</p><p>In 118 games with Triple-A Iowa, Murray hit .294/.395/.500 with 49 extra-base hits, 68 RBIs and 74 runs scored.</p><p>Murray, ranked as the organization’s No. 19 prospect, was a 15th-round draft choice of the Cubs in 2021.</p><p>He’ll become the second player born in the Bahamas to appear in a game for the Cubs, joining infielder <b>Andre Rodgers</b>, who played in nearly 500 games across four seasons as a North Sider in the 1960s.</p>

entries.title: Indiana's governor demands probe of power utility during tour of storm-ravaged Gary
entries.summary: <p>Brenda Medema grabbed lunch Monday afternoon at the American Red Cross Shelter inside the Hudson Campbell Sports and Fitness Center in downtown Gary.</p><p>The shelter became her home soon after a storm ripped through Northwest Indiana on Aug. 11.</p><p>“It’s been really tough," said Medema, 57. "I was getting heatstroke. I’ve been living in the shelter but the Red Cross makes it worth it."</p><p>Thousands lost power for days following the storm. While most have had it restored, dozens remained without power.</p><p>At the shelter, Indiana Gov. Mike Braun continued calls for a probe of the area's utility company after he made his tour of Gary. He also visited the area the day after the storm.</p><p>“We've never had this kind of an event in 100 years,” Braun said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" entries.title: Whole Foods planned for vacant Treasure Island building in Old Town
entries.summary: <p>A new Whole Foods Market is planned to open in Old Town, according to the neighborhood's alderperson. </p><p>The grocery store chain recently signed a lease at the former Treasure Island Foods location, 2nd Ward Ald. Brian Hopkins announced Monday in his weekly newsletter. The building at 1639 N. Wells St. has sat vacant since <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2018/9/29/18441977/chicago-grocery-chain-treasure-island-foods-to-shut-down-after-55-years" target="_blank" >Treasure Island closed in 2018</a>. </p><p>An opening date has not been determined, Hopkins said in a statement. </p><p>“From the beginning of the redevelopment review, I was clear that restoring a full-service grocery store to this location had to be a priority," he said. “Whole Foods Market is an established operator with the capacity to serve the neighborhood for the long term. There is still work ahead, but the signed lease is a concrete and welcome step forward.”</p><p>The grocery store chain also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/business/2026/04/20/whole-foods-grocery-store-wicker-park-lake-view" target="_blank" >plans to open stores</a> in the Wicker Park and Lake View neighborhoods.</p>
entries.author: Kaitlin Washburn

entries.title: White Sox manager Will Venable excited to bring Tommy Pham's trademark 'edge' to young, contending roster
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON – Right-hander <b>Tanner McDougal</b>, a preseason top-100 prospect per <i>Baseball America </i>capable of touching 100 mph, was in the visitor’s locker room at Daikin Park on Monday and will be activated on Tuesday as part of MLB rosters expanding to 28 players.</p><p>There’s more focus on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/31/tyler-schweitzer-tyler-gilbert-white-sox-davis-martin-will-venable-kyle-teel-ryan-fuller-astros-series-houston" target="_blank" ><u>the other player expected to join the Sox</u></a> on Tuesday: a 38-year-old platoon corner outfielder acquired from the Phillies Triple-A squad for cash.</p><p>Over his 13 MLB seasons, <b>Tommy Pham</b> has a career .796 OPS against left-handed pitching. He addresses a need for right-handed thump created when the Sox designated both <b>Everson Pereira</b> and <b>Austin Hays</b> for assignment within days of each other to make room trade-deadline acquisition <b>Brenton Doyle</b>; a glove-first center fielder.</p><p>The Sox have <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/21/white-sox-tristan-peters-second-half-slump-all-star-game-brenton-doyle-davis-martin-kyle-teel-will-venable-derek-shomon-mets-luis-robert-jr" target="_blank" ><u>plans for unlocking more offense from Doyle in the future</u></a>, but a long and durable offensive track record is the heart of Pham’s appeal. The 38-year-old is a .315/.331/.492 hitter in 37 career playoff games.</p><p>“He understands what it means to be in meaningful games down the stretch,” said manager <b>Will Venable</b>. “He knows what it means to play playoff games. He understands what it means to just perform and exist in high-leverage situations.”</p><p>Beyond the field, Pham is more famous both publicly and in league circles for his marked intensity. His 2024 stint with the White Sox is remembered less for him being the only Sox regular with an OPS over the league average, and more for him <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2024/06/02/tommy-pham-fighting-mad-after-white-sox-11th-straight-loss" target="_blank" ><u>overtly criticizing coaching decisions and touting his hand-to-hand combat skills</u></a> after an on-field dustup with Brewers All-Star catcher William Contreras after a grueling loss in Milwaukee.</p><p>Rather than worrying how Pham will mesh with his young roster and their deliriously goofy dugout hijinks, Venable is looking forward to it.</p><p>“One of my favorite players to coach,” said Venable, who overlapped with Pham as the Red Sox bench coach in 2022. “There’s a real value to how he approaches things, and that edge that he’s got is real. I think it also works in a lot of different types of environments; I think our environment, especially.”</p><p><b>Leasure out until 2028</b></p><p>Sox reliever <b>Jordan Leasure</b> faced a long road to recovery when he was sidelined with a flexor strain in late May. He’s now looking at an even longer one after undergoing surgery to repair a torn ulnar collateral ligament on Aug. 17. The Sox are hoping Leasure can return by spring 2028.</p><p>After undergoing his own UCL repair this spring, <b>Mike Vasil</b> is traveling to visit Dr. Keith Meister on Tuesday for a progress assessment. Pending approval, he should begin throwing mid-September.</p><p><b>This and that</b></p><p><b>Tyler Schweitzer </b>was activated from the paternity list Monday after missing this weekend’s series in Minneapolis. He has a 3.64 ERA in 29 2/3 innings of relief, and took <b>Tyler Gilbert</b>’s spot on the roster.</p><p>Rather than be a Sept. 1 addition, <b>Drew Thorpe</b> will start for Triple-A Charlotte on Wednesday.</p><p>The Sox also acquired veteran outfielder <b>Jake Cave</b> from the Rays for cash. Cave, 33, has not appeared in the majors since 2024.</p><p>A veteran of three separate Astros’ World Series runs, <b>Jose Urquidy </b>was greeted as a returning postseason hero in his first trip back to Houston since 2023.</p><p>“They [taught] me how to be a good professional baseball player,” Urquidy said. “And I’m very grateful.”</p>
entries.author: James Fegan
